descriptionChirho: A period of twelve months, used both in singular ('year,' 'a year') and plural ('years') to denote temporal duration in liturgical, narrative, and theological contexts—e.g., the high priest entering the Holy of Holies once a year (Heb 9:7, 9:25, 10:1, 10:3), the duration of a famine or drought (Luke 4:25; Jas 5:17), and prophetic time periods (Rev 9:15, Acts 18:11). The two clusters differ only in grammatical number: singular accusative/genitive (S67220) vs. plural accusative (S67221). Multilingual translations confirm uniformity: Spanish 'año/años,' Hindi 'वर्ष/वर्ष,' Arabic 'سَنَةِ/سِنينًا,' Korean '해의/해들을,' Swahili 'mwaka/miaka.'
